description: Dual-render workflow for every 3D design in Helping Hands. For each design, make (a) a three.js web concept render of the intended look and (b) the OpenSCAD part, exported to STL and loaded into the SAME viewer. Render both from the same fixed camera angles (front, side, top, iso, plus exploded) and put the pairs side by side, with a silhouette/overlay diff that highlights where they differ. Write a short 'differences and why' note per design (e.g. a printability constraint, a missing feature, wrong proportions) and the fix list. The OpenSCAD STL is the printable source of truth; the web render is the vision reference, not assumed correct. Show both on the Designs page cards (voice-0c526dc0). Apply it to the gripper generations and the Robot Glove Hand first. Make it one script: render_compare <design>.

results.notes: Jake: when he says 'work on <design>' (from any device), the Helping Hands Mac app comes forward full screen on that design: the web render large on one side and the OpenSCAD STL render beside it, from the same camera angles, and the diff on request. It must show the CURRENT state, even unfinished and while an agent is editing it: watch the design's files and live-reload both renders on every save. Add a helpinghands://designs/<name> URL plus a script (design.sh <name>) so the voice session opens it deterministically, and have the app list designs by name for fuzzy matching ('gripper', 'glove hand').

user_request.name: for any 3D thing, I want you to make the web render and then the 3D object render and then compare them. So then you can see where they differ and potentially why they differ

summary: Saying "work on <design>" should bring the Helping Hands Mac app forward full screen, showing the three.js web render beside the OpenSCAD STL render from matching camera angles, with a diff on request. Both renders must live-reload on every file save to show current unfinished state, and open via a helpinghands://designs/<name> URL and design.sh script with fuzzy name matching.
